clue.text: Epic drama about caring type

indicators.note: 'about' can mean around in every direction, so the letters are spun about into a new order

parts.note: both words taken as written, nine letters of fodder

explanation.surface: A sweeping stage epic is built around a character who looks after people.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambulance medic is someone whose job is looking after injured or sick people, a cryptic description of a carer.

clue.text: Nobles look mature

parts.note: to peer is to look closely
to age is to mature, grow older

explanation.surface: Aristocrats are being described as seeming grown-up and dignified.
explanation.definitionFit: The peerage is the collective body of titled lords and ladies, the British aristocracy taken as a whole.

clue.text: Sieve puzzle

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a coarse sieve for sorting gravel or grain
second meaning: a conundrum or enigma posed as a question

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the two words look like a single puzzle about sieves; they are two unrelated meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a coarse mesh tool for separating soil and a perplexing question with a clever solution.

clue.text: Value that's intrinsic to some rituals

indicators.note: something intrinsic is built into a thing, so the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A worth is said to be inherent in certain religious ceremonies.
explanation.definitionFit: Merit is worth or excellence, the quality of deserving praise, so it stands for value.

clue.text: End of second home racket

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: last letter of second
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: A second house turns out to be the end of a shady scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is a loud, unpleasant noise, and a din is exactly such a clamour.

clue.text: Sofa lifted! Cheers wildly

indicators.note: doing something wildly means doing it without order, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: both words taken as written, twelve letters of fodder

explanation.surface: Removal men hoist a couch and the crowd cheers them wildly.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chesterfield is a deep-buttoned leather couch with arms and back of equal height, a classic kind of settee.

clue.text: Hackneyed conclusion of tedious story

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: last letter of tedious
a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A dreary yarn ends with a clichéd ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Hackneyed ideas are overused and lacking freshness, like old bread gone dry and unappetising.

clue.text: Titian cast is wrong, figures expert

indicators.note: something wrong is out of its proper state, so the letters must be put into a different order

parts.note: the painter's name and the word cast taken as written
taken as written; it also serves the indicator phrase

explanation.surface: An art critic says the Venetian painter Titian's casting has been wrongly done, according to an expert.
explanation.walkthrough: Titian was a sixteenth-century Venetian painter. The word 'is' does double duty, supplying two letters while reading as part of the indicator phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A statistician works professionally with numerical data, so they are a specialist in numbers and their analysis.

clue.text: Perhaps Thunberg's performance, unconventional visit

parts.note: an act is a performance

indicators.note: unconventional means not in the usual form, so the letters are set out in an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written, fodder for the rearrangement

explanation.surface: Greta Thunberg's performance on an unusual trip is reviewed.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is', linking definition to wordplay. Greta Thunberg is the Swedish climate campaigner; 'Perhaps' marks her as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Greta Thunberg is a well-known climate campaigner, an example of someone campaigning vigorously for a political cause.

clue.text: Fortitude in finish: you organised church

parts.note: the end is the finish
U sounds like you, as in text speak
to run an event is to organise it
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone shows grit at the end, having organised a church event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' looks like an anagram signal but supplies a word of its own. CE stands for the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortitude is courage in bearing pain or hardship, which is the power of lasting through difficulty without giving up.

clue.text: Behind is displayed in daft error!

indicators.note: something displayed in a place is on show inside it, so the letters are found within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters span the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A silly mistake shows someone lagging behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Behind and the answer both describe position later in sequence or following at the rear.

clue.text: A levy reversed staff time for growth area

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: reversed means turned back to front, so the word before it is read from its end

parts.note: a toll is a levy or charge
men are the staff or workforce
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A tax cut is reversed, giving staff time for a growth sector.
explanation.walkthrough: An allotment is a rented plot of land in Britain where people grow their own vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: A rented garden plot is literally a patch of ground where vegetables and flowers are cultivated, a witty phrasing of growing space.

clue.text: Judgment by European: it's upset friend

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: A European's opinion has upset a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: An estimate is an approximate calculation or opinion, the valuation formed by judging rather than measuring.

clue.text: Wife wearing jeans turning to twirl

indicators.note: turning round means facing the other way, so the combined letters are read backwards
someone wearing clothes is inside them, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Levi's are a brand of jeans
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A wife in her jeans turns round to spin on the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: W goes inside LEVIS to make LEVIWS, which read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To twirl is to spin round quickly, the same motion as rotating on a pivot.

clue.text: Second coffee? Right

parts.note: a latte is a milky coffee
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone checks that a second cup of coffee is fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second coffee' looks like a request for another cup, but 'Second' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Of two things just mentioned, the second one is referred to by this word, as opposed to the former.

clue.text: Fantastic sea legs never getting any older

indicators.note: fantastic means fanciful and strange, so the letters take on an imaginative new arrangement

parts.note: both words taken as written

explanation.surface: An old sailor's marvellous balance on deck seems not to fade with the years.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that does not seem to age or show the passage of years stays youthful forever.

clue.text: Pointless dossier containing every other letter from cult

indicators.note: a thing containing something holds it inside, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a dossier is a file of documents

indicators.note: taking every other letter means keeping alternate ones and skipping the rest

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of cult

explanation.surface: An investigator's file on a cult turns out to be useless.
explanation.definitionFit: A futile effort achieves nothing, so it has no purpose or result.

clue.text: Milan team left huddle regularly for break

parts.note: Inter Milan is an Italian football club
L is the abbreviation for left

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter is kept

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters of huddle

explanation.surface: An Italian football side leaves its team huddle to take a breather.
explanation.walkthrough: Inter (Internazionale) is one of Milan's two big football clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: An interlude is an interval or pause between parts of a performance, so it is a rest period.

clue.text: Angry about having long limbs

indicators.note: 'about' can mean turned around, so the letters of the preceding word are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is cross about being lanky.
explanation.definitionFit: A rangy person or animal is tall and slim with long arms and legs, built for range of movement.

clue.text: Landlord's first moderate rental agreement

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: opening letter of Landlord's
to ease is to moderate or lessen

explanation.surface: A landlord offers a contract with fair terms to a tenant.
explanation.definitionFit: A lease is the legal contract by which a tenant rents property from its owner for a set term.

clue.text: One new currency unit, the writer's stimulus

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
N is the abbreviation for new
a cent is a small unit of money
the writer is I, and the writer's (has) becomes I've

explanation.surface: An author says a new coin gave them the spur to write.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The writer' is the setter, so it means I; with 's for 'has' it becomes I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: An incentive is something that motivates or encourages action, so it serves as a spur or motivation.

clue.text: Firm, western, milk supplier

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm
W is the abbreviation for western

explanation.surface: A firm in the west of the country supplies milk.
explanation.definitionFit: A dairy cow is the farm animal that produces milk, a playful description of the beast.

clue.text: Swiftness ultimately sees top bicycle take lead

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so the final letter of each following word is kept

parts.note: the final letters of the five words

explanation.surface: A cyclist sees the leading rider push ahead to take the lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Swiftness is quickness of movement, the rate at which something travels fast.

clue.text: Honeymooners, Lewis, Wendy, I missed out unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things going awry, so the remaining letters fall into a new order
something missed out is left out, so the named letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the letter to be removed

explanation.surface: Lewis and Wendy go on honeymoon, but the speaker sadly could not go.
explanation.definitionFit: A recently married couple on their post-wedding holiday are honeymooners, the classic picture of a just-wed pair.
